gaps.sentence: 'OK, I'll help you move house,' she said. She ___ to help me move house.
gaps.explanation: Agreement to a request is reported as agreed to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'Will you marry me?' he asked her. He asked her ___ marry him.
gaps.explanation: Will you...? → if/whether she would...: statement word order, backshifted modal.

gaps.sentence: He ___ me that the meeting had been cancelled.
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a personal object (told me); 'said me' is wrong, and speak/talk don't take that-clauses.

gaps.sentence: 'I saw her yesterday,' she said. She said she had seen her ___.
gaps.explanation: Yesterday becomes the day before (or the previous day) in reported speech.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
gaps.explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.

gaps.sentence: 'Do you know the way?' she asked me. She asked me ___ the way.
gaps.explanation: Do you know → if I knew: no do-support in the reported clause.

gaps.sentence: They ___ us that the museum had closed early.
gaps.explanation: Tell somebody (that)... — 'told' needs the direct personal object 'us'; 'said' cannot take it.

gaps.sentence: 'How long have you worked here?' she asked him. She asked him how long he ___ there.
gaps.explanation: have worked → had worked; 'here' becomes 'there' in reported speech.
